title: 'Francesco Rota' to 'Monsieur Vatron' in London, The Hague, 8 April 1624 (BSB Clm 10398 n. 106): letter key recovered from the leaf, code numbers open

documents.shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10398 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 48), n. 106, fol. 233r (MDZ bsb00116447 scan 469)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaf or beside it; the verso is blank and the neighbouring pieces are in clear.

transcription.source: MDZ IIIF image of the microfilm, bsb00116447 scan 469, 1216 x 1849 px, read on 4x crops
transcription.notes: One AI transcription, no second reader. 144 cipher tokens counted by decode.py (79 letter groups, 25 code numbers, 40 single signs); the --measure count of 294 includes the clear words.

system.summary: Clear Italian with two-digit numbers for single letters, written together and mixed with clear letters inside words; numbers with a tick above and numbers after a prefix letter g, c or m for names and words; single letters (q, t, p, z, x, r, n) standing alone for short words.

diacritics.note: a tick above some numbers and a bar above others; their meaning is not established

system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the two-digit letter numbers seen (25, of which 16 have a firm value). 20 and 70 may be second values for n and o (one use each), so homophones are not established.

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 2176 vetting of 4 Nov 2026: no DECODE record, nothing in Tomokiyo or Lasry, not printed in Rusdorf's Mémoires (1789), Goetz (Briefe und Akten N.F. II/1), Khevenhüller, Söltl, Gardiner or Krüner; Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955) not online and not seen. Issue #254: an earlier attack by Brice Dudout did not beat its shuffled-key control.

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau chose the target (catalogue 2176) and asked for a solution. Claude fetched the scan, transcribed, recovered the letter key, read and wrote up. No human checked the transcription or the reading.

solution.what: Scan 469 fetched from the MDZ IIIF server (bsb00116447), full size 1216 x 1849 px; scans 465-468 and 470-482 fetched to look for a key or a decipherment.
Line-by-line transcription from the scan and 4x crops; ticks and bars above numbers recorded; 4 and 7 told apart by form.
The two-digit numbers written together are single letters, mixed with clear letters inside words; ticked numbers and numbers after g, c, m are code words.

Words fixed by the clear text around them: discorre-32-do (n), peti-92 30 40-n (tio), 91 30 gli 40 22 90 (migliore), può 21 10 22 90 (fare), 10 81 92 22 40 (altro), 51 90 81 40 94 70 (geloso). Sixteen letter values decode 70 of 79 letter groups; 72 with 20 = n and 70 = o (one use each, plausible only).
Single signs from their sentences: q = che, t = non, p = per, p' = però, & = et; z = se plausible. x, r, n, m, pt and one more sign not resolved (x is a person or 'si').

Neighbouring pieces n. 105 and 107-112 (scans 465-490) opened for a key, a gloss or the same code: all in clear. Halm's catalogue searched as text: no other piece of the Rota correspondence is marked as cipher.

Halm 1874 searched through the MDZ text search ('Chiffern', 'chiffrirt', 'Rota', 'Hyacinth'): 13 pages mark cipher pieces, none of them another Rota or Hyacinth letter. n. 107, 108, 110, 111 read for names: g 27 may be Father Hyacinth and g 34 the Palatine or his house, from context only.
Decode built into Italian sentences and translated; 25 code numbers, 7 unticked numbers and 22 single signs stay open. 90 of 144 cipher tokens read (62.5%).

outcome.method_basis: Sixteen letter values recovered here from the leaf alone, using the clear Italian around and inside the cipher words; no key, decipherment or parallel text was available. The code numbers are not recovered.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py on transcription.txt: 144 cipher tokens (79 letter groups, 25 code numbers, 40 single signs); 72 letter groups and 18 signs read = 90/144.

credits.note: found the letter in the Munich Camerariana sweep (PR #242) and described its signs
showed that it is not the Camerarius 1621-22 code and that an attack on the numbers as a code fails (issue #254)

once each, no word fixed around them

gaps.detail: x is a person or 'si'; the page does not decide

texts.label: the letter, fol. 233r

reading_review.note: Read as sentences on 9 Nov 2026 by the AI that made the decode; no second reader. The clear text and the spelled words give sentences that construe as Italian and translate, but every sentence with cipher keeps at least one unread code number or sign, so the persons and subjects are missing: read in part, not read.

texts.summary: The writer, delayed at The Hague by an errand for the Nuncio in Amsterdam, reports that he pressed a person in code (g 34) hard and brought him to admit that nothing better exists for the greatness of his house, while the wife laughs at it. He asks his correspondent in London to maintain that he did not come there for a purpose that is in code, but for something else, and sends greetings to Father Anderson, the Count and a gentleman with a Capuchin beard. The persons and subjects in code are not read.

outcome.notes: Catalogue 2176. The catalogue's identifications (Rota = the Capuchin Alexander of Hales, from Goetz and Gardiner; Vatron perhaps Rusdorf) were not checked again here.
